content: 1. Tacrolimus may prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Rilpivirine should be used with caution when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 3. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of telavancin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Co-administration of rilpivirine with tetrabenazine, which also prolongs the QTc interval, is serious and should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 5. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of thioridazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of thiothixene by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Tipranavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 9. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of toremifene by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Tovorafenib decreases rilpivirine levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Co-administration of tovorafenib, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, with CYP3A substrates may lead to serious therapeutic failures. If unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of efficacy. 12. Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 13. Co-administration of antacids with rilpivirine may significantly decrease rilpivirine plasma concentrations due to increased gastric pH. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 14. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of trimipramine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ublituximab decreases the effects of rilpivirine through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Extreme caution should be exercised when vilanterol is co-administered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 18. Valbenazine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vandetanib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Voclosporin and rilpivirine may each increase the effects of the other by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Vonoprazan decreases rilpivirine levels or effects by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Voriconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. 24. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of voriconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vorinostat by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ziprasidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. In the general population, the estimated background rate for major birth defects in clinically recognized pregnancies is 2% to 4%, and the miscarriage rate is 15% to 20%. 28. Dolutegravir is present in human milk. It is unknown whether the components of this drug combination affect human milk production or have effects on breastfed infants. 29. When administered to lactating rats, rilpivirine was present in milk. Potential risks of breastfeeding include HIV-1 transmission (in HIV-1–negative infants), development of viral resistance (in HIV-1–positive infants), and adverse reactions in a breastfed infant similar to those seen in adults. 30. Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk, making the drug generally acceptable for use during pregnancy. 31. Rilpivirine is excreted in feces (85%, with 25% unchanged), while dolutegravir is excreted in feces (64%, with 53% unchanged). 32. Rilpivirine should be taken with a meal to optimize absorption. 33. Adding plans allows for comparison of formulary status with other drugs in the same class. 34. Formulary information may vary and is subject to change. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current information. 35.
